machine.note: The scored resource is NOT the host: replay_tenants.py is a discrete-event simulation in simulated time on a frozen fleet. Host facts are recorded only because the harness enforces a real wall-clock liveness budget (replay.py:36 DEFAULT_MAX_WALL_MS = 600000 ms) and a decide() budget (512/request).
machine.python: 3.10.9 (pure Python + PyYAML; no network, no GPU)
machine.host_wall_clock_per_train_replay_s: 4-40 s per tenant trace, far inside the 600 s budget; the host is not a bound

value.price: derived base rates, 8 open-weight models only

prime.price: derived base rates, all 12; the only provider with scheduled outages

fleet.quality: frozen ground-truth per-prompt per-model score matrix (matrix_tenant{A,B}_train.jsonl); the harness grades from req.quality, the router may not read it

scored_configuration.harness: evaluator/benchmark/replay_tenants.py, one tenant trace at a time
scored_configuration.split_measured_here: train only (trace_tenantA_train.jsonl n=2899, 51.4 min; trace_tenantB_train.jsonl n=1940, 47.4 min)
scored_configuration.outages: measured both with --split val (the two literal prime windows, 270 s total) and --split none; the val windows are the only outage schedule this run may see

bound.resource: the fleet's quality-versus-price frontier, read through an observable-feature quality estimator; secondarily prime's prefill throughput against tenant A's prompt-size tail, and the scheduled prime outages. Provider rate limits (RPM/TPM/concurrency) are NOT the binding resource in the scored per-tenant replay.
evidence: Where U goes, measured on train with outages (profiling/replays/): tenant A baseline U 0.5695 = quality 0.6212 - slo 0.0386 - 3*$0.004362. The cost term is worth only 0.0131 U at the baseline's spend and 0.0029 U at the absolute cost floor, so >95% of the achievable movement in U is quality selection and, for tenant A, the SLO term.

Information, not capacity, is the largest single term: with the SAME policy shape, an oracle that reads req.quality reaches U_A 0.8016 / U_B 0.5718, while the identical policy reading only the observable ridge head (req.features['prompt_id']) reaches U_A 0.6687 / U_B 0.4631. The 0.13 (A) and 0.11 (B) difference is pure quality information and is off limits (decision_log 'quality_information_source').

Rate limits barely bind when one tenant is replayed alone: ProbeOracleU on tenant A train issued 2937 decide() calls for 2899 requests, with 0 throttles_429 on all three providers; tenant A's 60 s peak of 240 arrivals is 34.2% of fleet RPM (42.1% with prime removed) and its peak token rate is 11.4% of fleet TPM. The env card's measured 19.4%-of-A-requests-throttled figure was taken on the MERGED trace; the scored replay is per tenant, so that contention is not in the score.

Tenant A carries a hard SLO floor from prefill throughput alone: prime (ttft_base 400 ms, prefill 60000 tok/s) can serve at most 126000 prompt tokens inside 2.5 s; 63 of 2899 train requests (2.17%) exceed that on EVERY provider at zero queue, so slo_violation_rate >= 0.0217 for tenant A no matter what the router does. The zero-queue optimum and both measured probes all land exactly on 0.0217 without outages.

The outage windows tighten that floor: without prime, the 2.5 s budget admits only 45000 prompt tokens (value) / 9600 (courier); 312 of 2899 tenant-A train requests (10.8%) arrive inside the 270 s of val windows and 20 of them (0.69% of the trace) become unservable-in-SLO for the duration. Measured cost of the windows: A 0.0217 -> 0.0259 slo rate and -0.008 U; B -0.003 U.
Tenant B has no SLO floor: its 600 s budget is met on every provider/model pair at zero queue (0 violations measured in every train replay, p95 169-210 s).

spec_sheet.unit: fleet requests/min (420 value + 132 prime + 150 courier), 20.5M tokens/min, 176 concurrent
spec_sheet.note: published provider tiers from env_card.yaml; not the binding limit here

achieved.unit: throttles_429 per tenant on the full train trace, all three providers, for the baseline and both ceiling probes

detail.single_provider_pressure: each tenant's 60 s peak is 160% (A) and 185% (B) of courier's RPM alone, so a cheapest-provider-only policy queues; spilling to value/prime removes the queue entirely

oracle_quality_ceiling_mean.method: per request, max over permitted models of the frozen req.quality dict, train split

cost_floor_usd_per_request.method: per request, min over (provider, permitted model) of (prompt_tokens*in + expected_output_tokens*out)/1e6 with the harness's own billing formula (replay_tenants.py TenantProvider.admit); prefix_tokens are 0 everywhere so no cache credit exists

cost_floor_worth_in_U.note: 3 * cost floor: driving cost to its floor is worth less than 0.003 U, so cost is a guard rail, not a lever

limit.method: All numbers from the train split only; no *_test.* file was opened and no val evaluation was spent. Analytic bounds: .skydiscover/llm-router/specification/profiling/fleet_bounds.py (single deterministic pass over both train traces against the frozen card). Reachable bounds: .skydiscover/llm-router/specification/profiling/probe_routers.py driven through the real harness, `python3 evaluator/benchmark/replay_tenants.py .data/traces/trace_tenant{A,B}_train.jsonl {evaluator.generic_policy.GenericPolicy|probe_routers.ProbeHeadU|probe_routers.ProbeOracleU} --split {val|none} --json`, 12 runs, all outputs in profiling/replays/. The replay is deterministic (sim_seed 11), so one sample per configuration is the measurement; every run reported violation_count 0 and aborted null.

ceiling.unit: U = mean_quality - 1.0*slo_violation_rate - 3.0*cost_usd_per_request, per tenant, train split, prime outage windows applied
ceiling.derivation: ACHIEVABLE ceiling, observable features only (the one that matters). Zero-queue per-request optimum under the shipped ridge head, argmax over (provider, permitted model) of qhat(m) - 3*cost(p,m,req) - 1[ttft/latency misses the SLO]: A 0.6795 (q 0.7237, $0.007499, slo 0.0217), B 0.4902 (q 0.5356, $0.015129, slo 0.0). Subtract the measured cost of rate limits, queueing and the prime outage windows, obtained by driving exactly that rule through the real harness (ProbeHeadU): A 0.6687 measured, B 0.4631 measured, i.e. the queue+outage tax is 0.011 U (A) and 0.027 U (B). Ceiling = the measured reachable value, rounded up to the zero-queue bound: A 0.669, B 0.462.

oracle_ceiling_unreachable.derivation: Same construction reading the ground-truth req.quality dict: zero-queue optimum A 0.8104 / B 0.6206, measured through the harness (ProbeOracleU, --split val) A 0.8016 (q 0.8382, $0.003573, slo 0.0259) / B 0.5718 (q 0.5938, $0.007331, slo 0.0). FORBIDDEN by decision_log 'quality_information_source'; recorded only as context. A candidate scoring above the achievable ceiling is reading req.quality and is a reward hack.

no_learning_floor.derivation: Best FIXED (provider, model) per observable cell (task x difficulty_hint decile), zero queue. A router with no per-prompt quality estimator cannot beat this; both values are BELOW the baseline, so the shipped ridge head is doing real work and a specialist must keep a per-prompt quality estimate.

tenant_A.derivation: 63/2899 train requests have prompt_tokens > 126000 = (2500 ms - 400 ms) * 60000 tok/s, prime's best case, so no provider can start their first token inside 2.5 s; +20 more arrive inside a prime outage window with prompt_tokens > 45000, value's best case. Worth 0.0259 U that no router can recover.

tenant_B.derivation: the 600 s budget is met by every provider/model pair at zero queue; measured 0 violations in all six tenant-B train replays

ceiling.unknowable: How much of the train ceiling transfers. The ridge head is fit IN-SAMPLE on the train matrices (baseline/train_generic.py:81-84), so train quality is optimistic. Measured shrink for the SAME policy at the SAME config, from the shipped baseline record (generic_baseline_results.json, read, not re-run, so no val evaluation was spent): tenant A U 0.5695 train -> 0.4361 val (-0.133), tenant B 0.3855 train -> 0.2702 val (-0.115). Expect the val-equivalent ceilings to be about A 0.54 and B 0.35. The transferable quantity is the GAP over the baseline, not the absolute level.

baseline_reference_point.source: re-measured here with evaluator/benchmark/replay_tenants.py on the train traces; the shipped evaluator/benchmark/baseline/generic_baseline_results.json reports VAL per-tenant numbers only, so it does not cover the train split and its val figures are quoted only for the train->val shrink estimate above

closable_gap.why_it_is_real: ProbeHeadU uses the SAME ridge head as the baseline, so none of this gap is extra information. It comes from three policy defects the probe fixes: (1) the baseline scores models with a per-model TRAIN-MEAN cost (generic_policy.py:59 self.mean_cost[m]) instead of this request's actual prompt_tokens/expected_output_tokens at this provider's price; (2) it picks the model first and the provider second, so it never trades a model against courier's 0.80x rates; (3) its lam=40 was tuned on merged traffic and is 13x the true cost weight of 3.0 in U, which buys cheapness the objective does not pay for. Tenant A must additionally keep its 2.5 s TTFT term (worth up to 0.017 U above the 0.0217 floor), tenant B has no SLO term at all and is a pure quality-per-dollar problem.
levers_ranked: A and B: score (provider, model) jointly with the request's own token counts at the true weight 3.0 USD^-1, not lam=40 against a per-model mean.
B: spend more, not less. The tenant-B ceiling costs $0.0151/request against the baseline's $0.0017; at 3 USD^-1 a cent of extra spend is worth 0.03 U and buys 0.145 mean quality.

A: prefer courier for the small-prompt bulk (median prompt_tokens 28, courier ttft 1702 ms fits 2.5 s) and reserve prime for the prompt-size tail; 5.59% of A's requests exceed courier's 9600-token TTFT budget and must not go there.

A: honour the announced outage (empty catalogue + outage_until) instead of retrying into it; the grace is 8 dispatches before outage_lost, and the 2000 ms retry_after alone exceeds 80% of the 2.5 s budget.

protocol.test_split: no *_test.* trace, matrix or manifest was read, opened, replayed or inspected
protocol.val_split: no val replay was run; generic_baseline_results.json was read as a shipped artifact, which is not one of the five logged val evaluations
